title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is an upside-down sheet of a Bourbaki typescript draft ('n° 413', page 1-47) that was reused as scrap paper. Its cross-references to 'Int. VII' (Bourbaki, Intégration ch. VII) and 'F. R. V.' (Fascicule de résultats, Variétés) mark it as a Bourbaki rédaction on Lie groups and manifolds over a complete valued field K. Section 16, 'Mesure de Haar d'une variété de groupe', works in a group manifold G of dimension n and class C^r, with local multiplication coordinates m_k(x;y) from (30).

1) The space Ω^n_e(G) of top-degree covectors at the identity e is one-dimensional. Hence the left-invariant n-forms form a line, spanned by the wedge of the left-invariant extensions I_g^{ω_k} of a basis ω_1, …, ω_n of Ω^1_e(G).

2) Taking ω_k = dx_k, a left-invariant top form near e is given by (31): I(x) = det(∂m_k/∂y_j(x^{-1};x)) dx_1…dx_n. This is the Jacobian at y = x of the left translation y ↦ x^{-1}y.

3) Right translations preserve the line of left-invariant n-forms. So R_y^* I = δ(y) I for a C^{r-1} function δ (32). Writing R_y = L_y ∘ Int(y^{-1}), and using that L_y^* acts trivially on left-invariant forms, gives δ(y) = det(Ad y)^{-1} (33).

4) For K locally compact, |I| is a left Haar measure. Locally, dμ = mod(det(...)) dx_1…dx_n (34), where mod is the module of K. The modular function of G is then Δ(y) = mod(det Ad y)^{-1} (35).

This is the standard result found in Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. III §3 n°16. It has no connection with the motivic and anabelian material on the surrounding Grothendieck pages.
errors: No mathematical errors. Formula (34) as typed has an unbalanced extra closing parenthesis, which is a typographical slip.
The formula Δ(y) = mod(det Ad y)^{-1} matches Bourbaki's convention for the modular function. Under the opposite convention it would read mod(det Ad y).

ideas.what: Left-invariant top forms on a Lie group over a valued field give left Haar measure via the module of K; explicit local expression via the Jacobian of multiplication
ideas.modern_name: Haar measure on p-adic/real Lie groups from invariant volume forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cartan, Weil); in this form, Bourbaki Lie III §3
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie ch. III §3 n°16 (a Bourbaki text, not Grothendieck's)

ideas.what: Modular function Δ(y) = mod(det Ad y)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Modular function of a Lie group

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused sheet of a Bourbaki draft (n° 413) giving the standard derivation of Haar measure and modular function on Lie groups over locally compact fields. It is unrelated to Grothendieck's motivic notes on the adjacent pages and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down (a reused Bourbaki typescript sheet). The machine transcription is essentially correct.
In (32), the left side I_g^ω(xy) denotes the form transported by right translation by y; the notation is the original typist's.
(34) contains an extra closing parenthesis in the original: 'mod(dét ∂m_k/∂y_j(x^{-1};x)))'.
The handwritten archive page number '217' (an earlier '412'/'417' is crossed out) appears at bottom left.
